It helps policymakers and investors make informed decisions by indicating the pace of economic expansion or contraction. **Source:** US BEA (table CAGDP1) [Download Data](data_download/gdpPercentChange.csv){download="gdpPercentChange.csv"} ::: ## ::: {.plot-space} ::: ```{r} #| label: Business Applications Change From a Year Ago #| echo: false #| message: false #| warning: false library(plotly) library(dplyr) biz <- readRDS("data/businessAppChange.rds") %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(date)) %>% filter(format(Date, "%Y") != "2006") %>% arrange(Date) biz <- biz %>% mutate( Date = as.Date(date), Year = format(Date, "%Y") ) # Get years years <- sort(unique(biz$Year), decreasing = TRUE) # Full date range all_date_min <- min(biz$Date, na.rm = TRUE) all_date_max <- max(biz$Date, na.rm = TRUE) # All Years button all_button <- list( method = "update", args = list( # Restore all data list( x = list( biz$Date, biz$Date ), y = list( biz$Michigan, biz$United_States ) ), # Restore full chart range list( title = "Percent Change in Business Applications", xaxis = list( range = c( all_date_min, all_date_max ) ) ) ), label = "All Years" ) # Year buttons year_buttons <- lapply(years, function(selected_year) { filtered_data <- biz %>% filter(Year == selected_year) date_min <- min( filtered_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE ) date_max <- max( filtered_data$Date, na.rm = TRUE ) list( method = "update", args = list( # Update data list( x = list( filtered_data$Date, filtered_data$Date ), y = list( filtered_data$Michigan, filtered_data$United_States ) ), # Update title and x-axis list( title = paste( "Percent Change in Business Applications:", selected_year ), xaxis = list( range = c( date_min, date_max ) ) ) ), label = selected_year ) }) # Combine All Years + individual years buttons <- c( list(all_button), year_buttons ) fig <- plot_ly(biz, x = ~Date) fig <- fig %>% add_lines( y = ~Michigan, name = "Michigan", line = list( color = "#004A5E" ), hovertemplate = paste( "%{x}
", "Michigan: %{y:.2f}%", "" ) ) fig <- fig %>% add_lines( y = ~United_States, name = "United States", line = list( color = "#AF2C32", dash = "dash" ), hovertemplate = paste( "%{x}
", "United States: %{y:.2f}%", "" ) ) fig %>% layout( title = list( text = "Percent Change in Business Applications
Michigan vs United States" ), xaxis = list( title = "", showline = TRUE ), yaxis = list( title = "Percent Change from Year Ago", zeroline = TRUE, zerolinecolor = "gray" ), legend = list( x = 1.05, y = 1, xanchor = "left" ), updatemenus = list( list( buttons = buttons, active = 0, x = 1.05, y = 0.7, xanchor = "left" ) ), shapes = list( # Great Recession list( type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper", x0 = "2007-12-01", x1 = "2009-06-01", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, fillcolor = "lightgray", opacity = 0.3, line = list(width = 0), layer = "below" ), # COVID recession list( type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper", x0 = "2020-02-01", x1 = "2020-04-01", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, fillcolor = "lightgray", opacity = 0.3, line = list(width = 0), layer = "below" ) ), margin = list( t = 60 ) ) %>% config(displayModeBar = FALSE) ``` ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"} ## Definition, Data Source and Download The percent change in business applications reflects entrepreneurial activity and economic dynamism. Read data pay <- readRDS("data/averageAnnualWage.rds") %>% mutate( year_MI = as.Date(paste0(year_MI, "-01-01")), value_MI = as.numeric(value_MI), value_US = as.numeric(value_US), industry = sub("^NAICS\\s+", "", seriesID) ) %>% arrange(industry, year_MI) # Industries in the order they appear in the data industries <- unique(pay$industry) # Initial industry init <- industries[1] df_init <- pay %>% filter(industry == init) # Create plot fig <- plot_ly() # Michigan trace fig <- fig %>% add_lines( data = df_init, x = ~year_MI, y = ~value_MI, name = "Michigan", line = list(color = "#004A5E") ) # United States trace fig <- fig %>% add_lines( data = df_init, x = ~year_MI, y = ~value_US, name = "United States", line = list(color = "#2B9CB4", dash = "dash") ) # Dropdown buttons buttons <- lapply(seq_along(industries), function(i){ df <- pay %>% filter(industry == industries[i]) list( method = "restyle", args = list( list( x = list( df$year_MI, df$year_MI ), y = list( df$value_MI, df$value_US ) ), c(0,1) ), label = industries[i] ) }) # Layout fig %>% layout( title = list( text = paste( "Average Annual Pay:", init ), x = 0.5, y = 0.88, xanchor = "center", yanchor = "top" ), xaxis = list( title = "", type = "date", tickformat = "%Y" ), yaxis = list( title = "Average Annual Pay", tickprefix = "$", tickformat = ",d", separatethousands = TRUE ), updatemenus = list( list( type = "dropdown", direction = "down", active = 0, buttons = buttons, x = 0.5, y = 1.25, xanchor = "center", yanchor = "top" ) ), legend = list( orientation = "h", x = 0.5, y = 1.08, xanchor = "center" ), shapes = list( list( type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper", x0 = "2020-02-01", x1 = "2020-04-01", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, fillcolor = "lightgray", opacity = 0.3, line = list(width = 0), layer = "below" ) ), annotations = list( list( x = "2020-03-01", y = 0.95, xref = "x", yref = "paper", text = "COVID Recession", showarrow = FALSE, font = list(size = 10) ) ), margin = list( t = 150, r = 40 ) ) %>% config(displayModeBar = FALSE) ``` ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"} ## Definition, Data Source and Download Tracking the average annual pay provides insights into income levels and purchasing power within an economy. It helps assess wage trends, labor market conditions, and overall economic well-being, guiding policymaking and business decisions. **Source:** BLS QCEW [Download Data](data_download/averageAnnualWage.csv){download="averageAnnualWage.csv"} ::: ## ::: {.plot-space} ::: ```{r} #| label: Per Capita Income #| echo: false #| message: false #| warning: false library(dplyr) library(knitr) library(htmltools) library(purrr) library(kableExtra) income <- readRDS( "data/PerCapitaIncome.rds" ) # Southwest Michigan county order county_order <- c( "Kalamazoo", "Berrien", "Branch", "Calhoun", "Cass", "St. Joseph", "Van Buren" ) # --------------------------------------------------------- # Create sparkline function # --------------------------------------------------------- make_sparkline <- function(values) { values <- as.numeric(values) # Remove missing values valid <- !is.na(values) if (sum(valid) < 2) { return("") } values <- values[valid] # Dimensions width <- 120 height <- 35 padding <- 3 # Scale values to chart dimensions x <- seq( padding, width - padding, length.out = length(values) ) value_range <- max(values) - min(values) if (value_range == 0) { y <- rep( height / 2, length(values) ) } else { y <- height - padding - ((values - min(values)) / value_range) * (height - 2 * padding) } # Create SVG line points <- paste( paste(x, y, sep = ","), collapse = " " ) # Return HTML SVG HTML( paste0( '' ) ) } # --------------------------------------------------------- # Create table data # --------------------------------------------------------- income_table <- income %>% mutate( # County ordering county_order = case_when( GeoName %in% county_order ~ match(GeoName, county_order), TRUE ~ length(county_order) + 1 ) ) %>% arrange( county_order, GeoName ) %>% mutate( # Formatted values `2024 Rank` = rank_2024, `Growth Rank` = pc_rank_2024, `2024 vs. 2023` = paste0( sprintf( "%.1f", pct_24_23 ), "%" ), Trend = pmap( list( DataValue_2020, DataValue_2021, DataValue_2022, DataValue_2023, DataValue_2024 ), ~ make_sparkline(c(...)) ) ) %>% select( GeoName, `2024 Rank`, `Growth Rank`, `2024 vs. 2023`, Trend ) # --------------------------------------------------------- # Render table # --------------------------------------------------------- htmltools::HTML( '

Per Capita Income by Michigan County

' ) htmltools::HTML( '
', '', '', '
' ) kable( income_table, format = "html", escape = FALSE, table.attr = 'id="incomeTable"', col.names = c( "County", "2024 Rank", "Growth Rank in State", "2024 vs. 2023

2020–2024" ), align = c( "l", "c", "c", "c", "c" ) ) %>% kable_styling( bootstrap_options = c( "striped", "hover", "condensed" ), full_width = FALSE ) ``` ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"} ## Definition, Data Source and Download The per capita income provides a measure of the average income earned per person, reflecting the economic well-being of residents.
